text:
aliya: Quick heads-up — for this month's recurring-pattern scan I pulled incidents from Jan/Feb/Mar and started a lightweight synthesis. High-level: two cascade signatures keep showing up (disk pressure -> eviction -> queued requests, and network flaps causing model fallback churn). Can folks add quick confirmations or counterexamples?

sam: Ack. I saw the disk-pressure chain in three Dedicated incidents. One was noisy GC on the allocator node.

noah: Agree on network. We had a cloud provider-level routing flap that caused health-check storms, autoscaler misinterpreted and triggered scale down.

lee: Is the GC one tied to long-tail batches or unusually large sequences? I remember one incident with 1M token batch.

sam: Not the 1M token one — that was separate. GC spikes correlated with concurrent per-tenant checkpoint writes + batch size ~ 256 on older CUDA driver nodes.

aliya: Good detail. I'm flagging two themes then: "storage/IO backpressure during checkpointing" and "control-plane vs data-plane network instability leading to cascade fallbacks".

noah: Suggestion: add one tactical action — pin checkpoint IO to lower priority cgroup and rate-limit checkpoint threads. Owner: sam. ETA: 2026-04-15.

sam: I can own the cgroup/rate-limit experiment. Will test on a Dedicated pool staging cluster.

lee: For the network case, ops-bot reported that retries were exponential but not jittered, causing sync pulses. Can we add jitter to retries and increase probe spread?

ops-bot: Auto-report: probe-schedule variance at incident 1768421009 was 0ms-10ms. Recommended: 20-200ms jitter.

eva: From product side, we need guardrails for fallbacks — can we add a soft-degradation policy that reduces max-concurrency before switching models? Owner: eva + noah. ETA: 2026-05-01.

aliya: Action items recap (please respond with :thumbsup: when you accept):
- sam: rate-limit/checkpoint cgroups + test on staging — ETA 2026-04-15
- noah + eva: soft-degradation policy + rollout plan — ETA 2026-05-01
- lee: review retry jitter and probe spread; update health-check docs — ETA 2026-04-10
- ops: add a recurring alert for "cascading fallbacks" pattern (>=3 fallbacks in 15m) — ETA 2026-04-05

sam: +1 :thumbsup:

noah: +1, I'll pair with eva on the API changes.

lee: On it, will PR health-check doc changes this week.

eva: Adding to roadmap mgmt board and linking postmortem tickets.

aliya: I'll populate the incidents tracking sheet with these action items and include the short query I used to surface patterns:```sql
SELECT incident_id, root_cause, tags, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY root_cause) as freq
FROM incident_events
WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01' AND created_at < '2026-04-01'
AND status = 'closed'
ORDER BY freq DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

noah: Nice — can you add the filter for deployment_type = 'dedicated' so we can separate hosted vs dedicated signals?

aliya: Good call, done in the sheet.

sam: One more note — let's categorize by cascade entry point (storage, network, scheduler, model oom) so we have cleaner action mapping.

aliya: Agreed. I'll add a column "cascade_entry" with values (storage|network|scheduler|model_oom|other).

lee: Can we have a brief follow-up sync in 2 weeks to review early experiment results?

aliya: Scheduling a 30m slot on 2026-04-08 10:00 PT and inviting participants. If that doesn't work I'll move it.

ops-bot: Reminder set: follow-up sync on 2026-04-08 10:00 PT.

eva: Thanks all — this is actionable and scoped.

aliya: Thanks — please update the sheet when you start work so I can track progress for the monthly incident patterns report.

sam: Will update once I have staging numbers.

noah: ETA acknowledged.

lee: Updating doc now.

ops-bot: Thread archived to incident-patterns index.
